translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Yangzhou rebel Li Zhichun's conspiracy was exposed, one of his followers had also been named Li Changzuo. Cheng Kegong and Grand Academician Liu Zhengzong drafted the rescript without clarifying the distinction;

sentences.zh: 又在吏部時，薦周亮工，擢至福建布政使，坐贓敗：克鞏疏引罪。

translations.literal: Also, while at the Board of Personnel, he had recommended Zhou Lianggong, who was promoted to Fujian Provincial Commissioner but fell on corruption charges: Kegong submitted a memorial accepting blame.
translations.idiomatic: While at the Board of Personnel he had also recommended Zhou Lianggong, who rose to Fujian Provincial Commissioner but was ruined by corruption. Cheng Kegong submitted a memorial taking blame.

sentences.zh: 左都御史魏裔介劾正宗，語連克鞏，並及昌祚、亮工事，克鞏疏辨，上責其巧飾，下王大臣議，罪當奪官。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie impeached Zhengzong, implicating Kegong in the same language and also touching on the Changzuo and Lianggong affairs; Kegong submitted a defense; the emperor rebuked him for specious argument and sent the matter to the princes and ministers for deliberation; the penalty was to be deprivation of office.
translations.idiomatic: Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie impeached Liu Zhengzong in terms that also implicated Cheng Kegong and raised the Changzuo and Lianggong affairs. Kegong defended himself, but the emperor rebuked his evasive pleading and referred the case to the princes and ministers, who found the penalty should be removal from office.

sentences.zh: 世祖初以克鞏世家子，知故事，不次擢用，值講筵，命內臣將畫工就邸舍圖其像以進，居常或中夜出片紙作國書詢時事，克鞏佔對惟謹；

translations.literal: At first the Shizu had exceptionally promoted Kegong as the son of an established family who knew precedent; during lecture sessions he ordered an inner eunuch to bring a painter to his residence to paint his portrait and present it; ordinarily he would sometimes at midnight send out a slip of paper with questions on affairs of state and current events, and Kegong would respond with scrupulous care;
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning the Shizu had promoted Cheng Kegong out of turn as the scion of a great family versed in precedent. During lecture sessions the emperor sent painters to his residence to paint his portrait. At times the emperor would send a note in the middle of the night with questions on affairs of state, and Kegong would answer with studied care;

sentences.zh: 至是，諭責其依違附和，凡事因人，仍寬之，命任事如故。

translations.literal: At this point, he was instructed and rebuked for equivocation and compliance, doing everything according to persons involved; still he was leniently treated and ordered to continue in office as before.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor rebuked him for equivocation and trimming, saying he shaped every decision to persons rather than principle, yet was lenient and ordered him to continue in office as before.

sentences.zh: 十八年，聖祖即位，復為國史院大學士。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the Shengzu ascended the throne, he was again made Grand Academician of the National History College.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, upon the Shengzu's accession, he was again made Grand Academician of the National History College.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，調秘書院大學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, he was transferred to Grand Academician of the Secretariat College.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi he was transferred to Grand Academician of the Secretariat College.

sentences.zh: 二年，乞休回籍。

translations.literal: In the second year, he requested retirement and returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he requested retirement and returned home.

sentences.zh: 克鞏迭主鄉、會試，稱得士，湯斌、馬世俊、張玉書、嚴我斯、梁化鳳等，皆出其門。

translations.literal: Kegong repeatedly presided over the provincial and metropolitan examinations and was said to have obtained good scholars; Tang Bin, Ma Shijun, Zhang Yushu, Yan Wosi, Liang Huafeng, and others all came from his school.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Kegong repeatedly presided over the provincial and metropolitan examinations and was reputed to pick the right men. Tang Bin, Ma Shijun, Zhang Yushu, Yan Wosi, Liang Huafeng, and others were all his protégés.

sentences.zh: 歷充太宗實錄，太祖、太宗聖訓總裁，屢得優賚。

translations.literal: He served successively as chief compiler of the Veritable Records of Taizong and the Sacred Instructions of Taizu and Taizong, and repeatedly received lavish rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief compiler of the Veritable Records of Taizong and the Sacred Instructions of Taizu and Taizong, and received repeated imperial rewards.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，太皇太后崩，赴臨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the Grand Empress Dowager died, he went to attend the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, when the Grand Empress Dowager died, he went to attend her funeral.

sentences.zh: 三十年，卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, he died at the age of eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he died at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 子亮，編修；

translations.literal: His son Liang was a Compiler;
translations.idiomatic: His son Liang served as Compiler;

sentences.zh: 光，武昌守道。

translations.literal: Guang was Intendant of Wuchang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Guang served as Intendant of Wuchang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 金之俊，字豈凡，江南吳江人。

translations.literal: Jin Zhijun, styled Qifan, was a native of Wujiang in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhijun, styled Qifan, came from Wujiang in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 明萬曆四十七年進士，官至兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Wanli of Ming he became a jinshi and rose to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi in the forty-seventh year of Wanli and rose to Vice Minister of War under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 睿親王定京師，命仍故官。

translations.literal: When Prince Rui secured the capital, he was ordered to retain his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Rui took Beijing, he was ordered to keep his former post.

sentences.zh: 疏請先蠲畿甸田租以慰民望，又言：「土寇率★降者，宜赦罪勿論。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting that land rents in the capital region first be remitted to satisfy popular hopes, and also said: "Bandits who generally surrender should have their crimes pardoned and not be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that land rents in the capital region should first be remitted to reassure the people, and added: "Bandits who generally surrender should be pardoned without prosecution.

sentences.zh: 縛渠來獻，分別敘功。

translations.literal: Those who bind and bring leaders to submit should be rewarded according to merit, separately assessed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who capture rebel leaders and surrender them should be rewarded according to their merit.

sentences.zh: 就撫之眾，宜編保甲，令安故業。

translations.literal: The masses who have submitted to pacification should be organized into baojia units and made to settle in their former occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered bands should be organized into baojia units and allowed to resume their former livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 無恆產者，別為區畫。」

translations.literal: Those without fixed property should be separately arranged."
translations.idiomatic: Those without steady property should be settled separately.

sentences.zh: 尋奏薦丁魁楚、丁啟睿、線國安、房可壯、左懋泰、郝絅等，又劾通州道鄭煇優游養寇、三關總兵郝之潤縱兵肆掠，俱宜罷斥；

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he submitted recommendations for Ding Kuitu, Ding Qirui, Xian Guo'an, Fang Kezhuang, Zuo Maotai, Hao Jiong, and others; he also impeached Tongzhou Circuit Intendant Zheng Hui for idly indulging bandits and Three Passes Commander-in-Chief Hao Zhirun for letting his troops plunder at will; all should be dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: He soon recommended Ding Kuitu, Ding Qirui, Xian Guo'an, Fang Kezhuang, Zuo Maotai, Hao Jiong, and others, and impeached Tongzhou Circuit Intendant Zheng Hui for coddling bandits and Three Passes Commander Hao Zhirun for letting his troops plunder freely—all deserving dismissal.

sentences.zh: 並請趣畿南北巡按及監司以下官赴任，禁止滿洲官役額外需索驛遞夫馬。

translations.literal: He also requested that surveillance commissioners north and south of the capital region and officials from provincial commissioners downward be urged to take up their posts, and that Manchu officials and runners be forbidden from making extra demands on courier stations for horses and porters.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that surveillance commissioners throughout the capital region and all officials down to circuit-level be urged to take office, and that Manchu officials and runners be barred from extorting extra horses and porters from courier stations.

sentences.zh: 疏入，皆採行。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, all its proposals were adopted and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and all its proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，以京師米貴，疏言：「大兵直取江南，應令漕督及巡漕御史赴任。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, because rice in the capital was dear, he submitted a memorial saying: "The main army will strike directly at Jiangnan; the Grain Transport Director and Surveillance Censor for Grain Transport should be ordered to take office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi, with rice scarce in the capital, he memorialized: "With the main army pushing directly into Jiangnan, the Grain Transport Director and the Surveillance Censor for Grain Transport should be ordered to take up their posts.

sentences.zh: 金陵底定，舉行漕政。」

translations.literal: Once Jinling is settled, grain transport administration should be put in operation."
translations.idiomatic: Once Nanjing is pacified, grain transport administration should be put in place.

sentences.zh: 詔速議行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered speedy deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered immediate deliberation and action.

sentences.zh: 因復上漕政八事，疏下所司。

translations.literal: Thereupon he again submitted eight items on grain transport policy; the memorial was sent down to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted eight further proposals on grain transport, and the memorial was referred to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 尋調吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 三年，疏請酌定進士銓選之制。

translations.literal: In the third year, he submitted a memorial requesting that the system for selecting jinshi be carefully established.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he memorialized for a regulated system of jinshi appointment.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 六年，乞假歸，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he requested leave to return home and was given the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he took leave to return home and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 七年，還朝。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 八年，調兵部，加少保兼太子太保。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was transferred to the Board of War and given the titles Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to the Board of War and made Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十年，調左都御史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「審擬盜犯，請用正律，不宜概行籍沒，致累無辜。」

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "In trying and sentencing robbery offenders, the regular statutes should be applied; wholesale confiscation of property should not be carried out, lest the innocent be harmed."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Robbery cases should be tried under the regular statutes. Property should not be confiscated wholesale, lest innocent families be ruined.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「直省提學，例以僉事道分遣。

translations.literal: He submitted another memorial saying: "Educational commissioners in the provinces are customarily dispatched as judicial-assistant circuit officials.
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he wrote: "Provincial educational commissioners are customarily dispatched as judicial-assistant circuit officials.

sentences.zh: 畿輔為首善之區，江南人才之會，請以翰林官簡用。」

translations.literal: The capital region is the chief seat of refinement, and Jiangnan is the gathering place of talent; Hanlin officials should be selected and appointed."
translations.idiomatic: But the capital region is the premier seat of learning and Jiangnan the greatest pool of talent. I ask that Hanlin officials be selected for these posts.

sentences.zh: 均報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 尋遷吏部尚書，授國史院大學士。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was transferred to Minister of Personnel and appointed Grand Academician of the National History College.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Minister of Personnel and Grand Academician of the National History College.

sentences.zh: 十二年，之俊病，乞​​休，上不允，遣畫工就邸畫其像。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Zhijun fell ill and requested retirement; the emperor did not consent and sent a painter to his residence to paint his portrait.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Zhijun fell ill and asked to retire. The emperor refused and sent a painter to his residence to paint his portrait.

sentences.zh: 十三年，諭諸大臣曰：「君臣之義，終始相維。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he instructed the ministers, saying: "The bond between ruler and minister is one of mutual dependence from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the emperor addressed the ministers: "The bond between ruler and minister is one of mutual devotion from first to last.

sentences.zh: 爾等今後毋以引年請歸為念。

translations.literal: You hereafter must not set your minds on citing age to request return home.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter you must not dwell on citing your years as grounds for retirement.

sentences.zh: 爾等豈忍違朕，朕亦何忍使爾等告歸？

translations.literal: Can you bear to go against me? And how could I bear to let you announce your return home?
translations.idiomatic: Would you truly abandon me? And how could I bear to send you home?

sentences.zh: 昨歲之俊病甚，朕遣人圖其容。

translations.literal: Last year Zhijun was gravely ill; I sent someone to paint his likeness.
translations.idiomatic: Last year Zhijun was gravely ill, and I sent someone to paint his likeness.

sentences.zh: 念彼已老，惟恐不復相見，不勝眷戀。

translations.literal: Thinking how old he was, I feared we might never meet again and was overcome with affection.
translations.idiomatic: He was so old that I feared we might never meet again, and my heart was full of longing.

sentences.zh: 朕簡用之人，欲皓首相依，不忍離也！」

translations.literal: The men I have chosen I wish to keep beside me with white hair together—I cannot bear to part!"
translations.idiomatic: The men I have chosen I wish to keep at my side until our hair is white together. I cannot bear to let you go!

sentences.zh: 之俊泣謝。

translations.literal: Zhijun wept and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun wept and thanked him.

sentences.zh: 十五年，改中和殿大學士，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was transferred to Grand Academician of the Zhonghe Hall and concurrently Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made Grand Academician of the Zhonghe Hall and concurrently Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 同校定律例。

translations.literal: He jointly collated the legal code.
translations.idiomatic: He helped collate the legal code.

sentences.zh: 十六年，詔立明莊烈帝碑，命之俊撰文。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, an edict ordered the erection of a stele to the Ming Chonglie Emperor, and Zhijun was ordered to compose the inscription.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year an edict ordered a stele erected to the Chonglie Emperor of the Ming, and Zhijun was commanded to write the text.

sentences.zh: 尋加太保兼太子太師，复乞假歸。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was made Grand Guardian and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and again requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Guardian and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and again asked leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 十七年，自陳乞罷，溫諭敦召，未至，加太傅。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he offered himself for dismissal; a gracious edict urgently summoned him; before he arrived, he was given the title Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he offered his resignation. A warm edict urgently recalled him. Before he could return, he was made Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 十八年，復改秘書院大學士。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was again transferred to Grand Academician of the Secretariat College.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was again made Grand Academician of the Secretariat College.

sentences.zh: 之俊自歸後，屢以衰老乞休，康熙元年，始允致仕。

translations.literal: After Zhijun returned home, he repeatedly requested retirement on grounds of age; in the first year of Kangxi, he was at last permitted to resign.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home Zhijun repeatedly pleaded age as grounds for retirement. In the first year of Kangxi he was finally allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 之俊家居，有為匿名帖榜其門以謗之者，之俊白總督郎廷佐窮治之，牽累不決。

translations.literal: While living at home, Zhijun had someone post an anonymous libel at his gate to slander him; Zhijun reported this to Governor-General Lang Tingzuo to investigate thoroughly, but the affair dragged on without resolution and many were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: At home Zhijun found an anonymous libel posted on his gate. He reported it to Governor-General Lang Tingzuo for a thorough investigation, but the case dragged on inconclusively and many were implicated.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上不直所為，以律禁收審匿名帖，鐫廷佐二級，之俊削太傅銜。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, the emperor did not approve of the conduct; citing the law forbidding investigation of anonymous libels, he demoted Tingzuo two ranks and stripped Zhijun of his Grand Mentor title.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair reached the emperor, he disapproved. Citing the law forbidding prosecution on the basis of anonymous postings, he demoted Lang Tingzuo two ranks and stripped Zhijun of his Grand Mentor title.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，諡文通。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he died and was posthumously titled Wentong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died and was given the posthumous title Wentong.

sentences.zh: 謝升，山東德州人。

translations.literal: Xie Sheng was a native of Dezhou in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Sheng came from Dezhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 明萬曆三十五年進士，官至建極殿大學士，兼吏部尚書，加少保兼太子太保。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Wanli of Ming he became a jinshi and rose to Grand Academician of the Jianji Hall, concurrently Minister of Personnel, with the titles Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi in the thirty-fifth year of Wanli and rose to Grand Academician of the Jianji Hall, concurrently Minister of Personnel, with the titles Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 崇禎之季，明帝欲與我議和，升洩其語，罷歸里。

translations.literal: In the last years of Chongzhen, the Ming emperor wished to discuss peace with us; Sheng leaked his words, was dismissed, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen's final years the Ming emperor sought peace with the Qing. Xie Sheng leaked the overture, was dismissed, and retired home.

sentences.zh: 李自成入京師，升與明御史趙繼鼎、盧世㴶逐自成所置吏，奉明宗室香河知縣師敔城守。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng entered the capital, Sheng, together with Ming censor Zhao Jiding and Lu Shijie, drove out the officials Li Zicheng had installed and, supporting Ming imperial clansman Shi Yi, magistrate of Xianghe, held the city in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng took Beijing, Xie Sheng, with the Ming censor Zhao Jiding and Lu Shijie, expelled Li's appointees and rallied behind the Ming clansman Shi Yi, magistrate of Xianghe, to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 尋奉表來歸，授師敔知州，命升以建極殿大學士管吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he submitted a memorial submitting to allegiance; Shi Yi was appointed prefect; Sheng was ordered to serve as Grand Academician of the Jianji Hall overseeing the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted his allegiance. Shi Yi was made prefect, and Xie Sheng was ordered to serve as Grand Academician of the Jianji Hall in charge of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 升至京師，改命與諸大學士共理機務。

translations.literal: When Sheng reached the capital, his appointment was changed: he was ordered together with the other grand academicians to manage state affairs jointly.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Sheng reached Beijing, his orders were changed: he was to manage state affairs jointly with the other grand academicians.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，卒，贈太傅，諡清義。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, he died and was posthumously granted the title Grand Mentor with the posthumous name Qingyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi he died and was posthumously made Grand Mentor with the posthumous title Qingyi.

sentences.zh: 胡世安，四川井研人。

translations.literal: Hu Shi'an was a native of Jingyan in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shi'an came from Jingyan in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎元年進士，官至少詹事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen of Ming he became a jinshi and rose to Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi in the first year of Chongzhen and rose to Junior Mentor under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 順治初，授原官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi, he was granted his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shunzhi reign he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 四遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In four promotions he reached Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted four times to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授武英殿大學士，兼兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was appointed Grand Academician of the Wuying Hall and concurrently Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made Grand Academician of the Wuying Hall and concurrently Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 聖祖即位，與之俊同改秘書院大學士。

translations.literal: When the Shenzu ascended the throne, he and Zhijun were both reassigned as Grand Secretaries of the Secretariat College.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shenzu took the throne, he and Zhijun were both transferred to Grand Secretary of the Secretariat College.

sentences.zh: 以疾乞休，累加少師兼太子太師。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he requested retirement and was repeatedly promoted to Junior Preceptor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire because of illness and was successively promoted to Junior Preceptor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 王永吉，字修之，江南高郵人。

translations.literal: Wang Yongji, styled Xiuzhi, was a native of Gaoyou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yongji, whose style name was Xiuzhi, came from Gaoyou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 明天啟間進士，官至薊遼總督。

translations.literal: During the Ming Tianqi reign he became a jinshi and rose to Governor-General of Jizhou and Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi under the Ming during the Tianqi reign and eventually served as Governor-General of Jizhou and Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，以順天巡撫宋權薦，授大理寺卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, on the recommendation of Shuntian Governor Song Quan, he was appointed Chief Justice of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi, on Song Quan's recommendation as Shuntian governor, he was made Chief Justice of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 永吉疏辭，上責其博虛名，特允之，並諭永不錄用。

translations.literal: Yongji memorialized to decline the appointment; the emperor rebuked him for courting empty fame, specially granted his request, and ordered that he never be employed again.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji submitted a memorial declining the post. The emperor accused him of seeking hollow reputation, granted the request as an exception, and declared that he would never again be appointed to office.

sentences.zh: 居數年，有詔起用廢員，复詣京師，吏部疏薦，八年，授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: After several years at home, an edict ordered the reinstatement of dismissed officials; he returned to the capital, the Board of Civil Appointments memorialized recommending him, and in the eighth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later an edict called dismissed officials back into service. He went to the capital again, the Board of Civil Appointments recommended him, and in the eighth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 條奏各衛所屯地分上、中、下三等，請撥上田給運丁；

translations.literal: In a detailed memorial he proposed dividing garrison colony lands of the guards and battalions into upper, middle, and lower grades and allocating the best fields to transport conscripts;
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a detailed memorial proposing that garrison colony lands be graded upper, middle, and lower, with the best plots assigned to grain-transport laborers;

sentences.zh: 各項折色銀請仍令官收官解，本色物料動支折價採買；

translations.literal: for all commuted silver payments he requested that officials again collect and deliver tribute as before, while physical materials in kind should be procured by drawing on commuted-value funds;
translations.idiomatic: that commuted silver payments continue to be collected and delivered by officials, while materials owed in kind be purchased with funds drawn from commuted payments;

sentences.zh: 洲田丈量累民，請以蘆課併入州縣考成，五年一次丈量：皆見採擇。

translations.literal: measuring sandbar fields burdened the people, so he requested merging the reed tax into county performance evaluations and surveying once every five years: all these proposals were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: and that the burden of surveying sandbar fields be eased by folding the reed tax into county performance reviews and remeasuring only once every five years. All of these proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 永吉家居，究心黃河下游閼壅為害，嘗議修涇河閘，濬射陽湖。

translations.literal: While living at home, Yongji devoted himself to the harm caused by downstream blockages of the Yellow River and once proposed repairing the sluice on the Jing River and dredging Lake Sheyang.
translations.idiomatic: While at home Yongji studied the damage caused by blockages on the lower Yellow River and once proposed repairing the Jing River sluice and dredging Lake Sheyang.

sentences.zh: 九年，疏言：「黃水自邳、宿下至清河口，淮、泗之水聚於洪澤湖，亦出清河口。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he memorialized, saying: "Yellow River water flows from Pi and Su down to Qinghe Mouth; the waters of the Huai and Si gather in Hongze Lake and also issue from Qinghe Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he memorialized: "The Yellow River runs from Pi and Su down to Qinghe Mouth. The Huai and Si rivers converge in Hongze Lake and likewise discharge at Qinghe Mouth.

sentences.zh: 二水交會，淮、泗弱勢，不能敵黃。

translations.literal: Where the two waters meet, the Huai and Si are weaker and cannot withstand the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Where the two currents meet, the weaker Huai and Si cannot hold back the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 折而南趨四百餘裡，出瓜洲、儀真方能達江。

translations.literal: Turning south it runs more than four hundred li before reaching the Yangtze only through Guazhou and Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: It turns south and runs more than four hundred li before it can reach the Yangtze only by way of Guazhou and Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 一線運河，收束甚緊，即有大小閘洞宣洩，海口不開，下流壅滯，以致河堤十年九決。

translations.literal: The Grand Canal is a single narrow channel, tightly confined; even with large and small sluice gates for discharge, if the river mouth is not opened the lower course becomes blocked, so that dikes break nine years out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Canal is a single narrow channel under heavy constraint. Even with large and small sluice gates to release water, if the river mouth stays closed the lower course backs up and the dikes break nine years in ten.

sentences.zh: 海口在興化、泰州、鹽城境內，輒為附近居民填塞。

translations.literal: The river mouth lies within Xinghua, Taizhou, and Yancheng, yet nearby residents repeatedly fill it in.
translations.idiomatic: The river mouth lies in Xinghua, Taizhou, and Yancheng, yet local residents repeatedly choke it off.

sentences.zh: 乞敕河、漕重臣相度疏濬，復其故道。

translations.literal: I beg that high officials of river control and grain transport be ordered to survey the terrain, dredge the channel, and restore its former course.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that senior officials responsible for river control and grain transport be ordered to survey the ground, dredge the channel, and restore its old course.

sentences.zh: 淮、泗消則黃河勢亦減。」

translations.literal: If the Huai and Si are relieved, the force of the Yellow River will also diminish."
translations.idiomatic: If the Huai and Si are relieved, the force of the Yellow River will diminish as well."

sentences.zh: 時河以北諸省患水，而江以南又苦旱，屢詔蠲賑，而湖廣、四川、閩、廣諸鎮待餉甚急。

translations.literal: At that time the provinces north of the river suffered from flooding, while south of the Yangtze they suffered drought; edicts repeatedly remitted taxes and provided relief, yet the garrisons of Huguang, Sichuan, Fujian, and Guangdong urgently awaited pay.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the provinces north of the river were afflicted by flood, while south of the Yangtze they suffered drought. Edicts repeatedly granted tax relief and famine aid, yet garrisons in Huguang, Sichuan, Fujian, and Guangdong were in urgent need of supplies.

sentences.zh: 永吉疏請下廷臣籌足餉救荒之策，上命永吉詳具以聞。

translations.literal: Yongji memorialized asking that court officials be convened to devise measures to secure pay and relieve famine; the emperor ordered Yongji to submit a detailed plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji memorialized asking that court officials be summoned to devise ways to secure pay and relieve famine. The emperor ordered Yongji to submit a detailed proposal.

sentences.zh: 永吉因言：「各省兵有罪革佔冒，馬亦有老病弱斃，十汰其二。

translations.literal: Yongji then said: "In each province soldiers guilty of fraudulent enrollment should be dismissed, and among the horses there are also old, sick, weak, and dead ones; eliminate two out of every ten.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji then wrote: "In every province soldiers found guilty of fraudulent enrollment should be dismissed, and among the horses there are old, sick, weak, and dead animals as well; cut two out of every ten.

sentences.zh: 以百萬之餉計之，歲可省二十萬。

translations.literal: Calculated on a pay budget of one million taels, two hundred thousand could be saved each year.
translations.idiomatic: On a pay budget of one million taels, two hundred thousand could be saved each year.

sentences.zh: 即以裁省之項，酌定直省災​​傷分數，則兵清而賦亦減。」

translations.literal: The savings could then be applied to set disaster-damage percentages for the metropolitan provinces, so that the army would be cleaned up and tax burdens reduced as well."
translations.idiomatic: Those savings could then be used to set disaster-relief percentages for the metropolitan provinces, clearing out the army while easing tax burdens as well."

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the proposal and approved it.

sentences.zh: 畿輔奸民，每藉投充旗下，橫行骫法。

translations.literal: Wicked people in the capital region constantly relied on enrolling under the banners to act outrageously and bend the law.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked men in the capital region routinely enrolled themselves under the banners and then acted with impunity, evading the law.

sentences.zh: 永吉疏陳其害，謂：「上乾國法，下失人心，請敕禁王大臣濫收人投旗，以息諸弊。」

translations.literal: Yongji memorialized setting forth the harm and said: "Above it violates state law, below it loses the people's hearts. I request an edict forbidding princes and high ministers to accept people into their banners indiscriminately, so that these abuses may cease."
translations.idiomatic: Yongji memorialized on the harm, writing: "Above it violates the law of the state; below it alienates the people. I ask that princes and high ministers be forbidden to accept people into their banners indiscriminately, so that these abuses may cease."

sentences.zh: 十年，擢兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十一年，與刑部尚書覺羅巴哈納等分賑直隸八府。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, together with Minister of Justice Jueluo Bahana and others, he distributed famine relief across the eight prefectures of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he joined Minister of Justice Jueluo Bahana and others in distributing famine relief across the eight prefectures of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 轉都察院左都御史，擢秘書院大學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate and then promoted to Grand Secretary of the Secretariat College.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate and then promoted to Grand Secretary of the Secretariat College.

sentences.zh: 永吉在兵部，鞫德州諸生呂煌匿逃人行賄，讞未當，下王大臣詰問，永吉厲聲爭辨。

translations.literal: While Yongji was at the Ministry of War, he tried the Dezhou scholar Lü Huang for harboring fugitives and taking bribes; the verdict was deemed inappropriate, the case was sent down to princes and high ministers for questioning, and Yongji argued loudly in his own defense.
translations.idiomatic: While serving at the Ministry of War, Yongji tried the Dezhou scholar Lü Huang for harboring fugitives and accepting bribes. When the verdict was judged improper and the case was referred to princes and high ministers for questioning, Yongji argued back in a loud voice.

sentences.zh: 事聞上，諭曰：「永吉破格超擢，當竭力為國，乃因詰問，輒至忿怒，豈欲效陳名夏故態耶？」

translations.literal: When the affair reached the emperor, he instructed: "Yongji was promoted beyond convention and ought to exert himself for the state, yet because of questioning he flew into anger. Does he mean to imitate Chen Mingxia's old behavior?"
translations.idiomatic: When the matter reached the emperor, he said: "Yongji was promoted beyond the usual limits and ought to serve the state with all his strength, yet at the first questioning he grew furious. Does he mean to repeat Chen Mingxia's old conduct?"

sentences.zh: 左授倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: He was demoted and reassigned as Vice Minister of the Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Vice Minister of the Granary.

sentences.zh: 十二年，仍授國史院大學士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was again appointed Grand Academician of the National History College.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was again appointed Grand Academician of the National History College.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子太保，領吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and placed in charge as Minister of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and placed in charge as Minister of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 十四年夏，旱，疏請「下直省督、撫、按諸臣清釐庶獄，如有殊常枉屈，奏請上裁；

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourteenth year, during drought, he memorialized requesting "that governors-general, governors, and provincial surveillance commissioners of the metropolitan provinces be ordered to clear up ordinary cases; where there are exceptional wrongs, they should memorialize for the emperor's decision;
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourteenth year, during a drought, he memorialized asking "that governors-general, governors, and provincial surveillance commissioners across the provinces review ordinary cases; where there were exceptional injustices, they should report them for the emperor's decision;

sentences.zh: 贖徒以下，保釋寧家」。

translations.literal: and redeemable convicts and those below them be released on bail to return home."
translations.idiomatic: and redeemable convicts and lesser offenders be released on bail to return home."

sentences.zh: 下所司議行。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the responsible offices for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the responsible offices for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 旋以地震具疏引咎，上复責其博虛名。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, citing the earthquake, he submitted a memorial accepting blame; the emperor again rebuked him for courting empty fame.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, citing the earthquake, he submitted a memorial accepting blame. The emperor again accused him of seeking hollow reputation.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以兄子樹德科場關節事發，左授太常寺少卿，遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, because his nephew Shude was implicated in an examination-hall collusion affair, he was demoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and then transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, after his nephew Shude was caught up in an examination collusion scandal, he was demoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and then transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year.

sentences.zh: 上以永吉勤勞素著，命予優恤，贈少保兼太子太保、吏部尚書，諡文通。

translations.literal: Because Yongji's diligence and service had long been notable, the emperor ordered generous posthumous honors: he was granted Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Civil Appointments, with the posthumous name Wentong.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yongji's long record of diligent service was well known, the emperor ordered generous posthumous honors, granting him Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Civil Appointments, with the posthumous name Wentong.

sentences.zh: 黨崇雅，陝西寶雞人。

translations.literal: Dang Chongya was a native of Baoji in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Chongya came from Baoji in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 明天啟五年進士，官至戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqi of Ming he became a jinshi and rose to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi in the fifth year of Tianqi under the Ming and rose to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，以天津總督駱養性薦，授原官，調刑部。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, on the recommendation of Tianjin Governor-General Luo Yangxing, he was granted his former office and transferred to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi, on Luo Yangxing's recommendation as Tianjin governor-general, he was restored to his former rank and transferred to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「舊制，大逆大盜，決不待時，餘俱監候秋後處決，未嘗一罹死刑，輒棄於市。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Under the old system, for great treason and great robbery execution was not delayed; all others were held in prison awaiting autumn execution. It was never the case that as soon as one incurred the death penalty he was immediately exposed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Under the old system, those guilty of great treason or great robbery were executed without delay; all others were held in prison until autumn execution. No one was ever put to death and immediately exposed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 請凡罪人照例區別，以昭欽卹。

translations.literal: I request that all offenders be distinguished according to precedent, so as to display imperial clemency.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that offenders be distinguished according to precedent, so that imperial clemency may be made clear.

sentences.zh: 新制未定，並乞暫用明律。

translations.literal: Since the new code is not yet settled, I also beg that the Ming code be temporarily applied.
translations.idiomatic: Since the new code is not yet settled, I also ask that the Ming code be used for the time being.

sentences.zh: 俟新例頒行，畫一遵守。」

translations.literal: When the new regulations are promulgated, they should be uniformly obeyed."
translations.idiomatic: Once the new regulations are issued, they should be followed uniformly."

sentences.zh: 二年，复疏言：「流寇暴虐，今剿滅殆盡。

translations.literal: In the second year he again memorialized, saying: "The roving bandits were savage and cruel, but now they have been nearly exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he memorialized again: "The roving bandits were savage, but they have now been nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 恐寇黨株連，下民未獲寧止。

translations.literal: I fear that through guilt by association with the bandit factions the common people have not yet found peace.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that through guilt by association with the bandits the common people still cannot live in peace.

sentences.zh: 請速頒恩赦。

translations.literal: I request that an amnesty be quickly promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that an amnesty be issued at once.

sentences.zh: 督、撫、司、道及府、州、縣各官，簡用務在得人，庶可廣皇仁，布實政。」

translations.literal: Governors-general, governors, provincial and circuit officials, and officials of prefectures, departments, and counties should be carefully selected with the aim of getting the right men, so that imperial benevolence may be broadly extended and real governance put into practice."
translations.idiomatic: Governors-general, governors, provincial and circuit officials, and prefectural, departmental, and county officers should be carefully chosen so that the right men are found, thereby extending imperial benevolence and putting honest governance into practice."

sentences.zh: 並得旨允行。

translations.literal: Imperial approval was granted and the proposals were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposals and they were carried out.

sentences.zh: 駱養性被訐貪婪通賊，辭連崇雅，讞不實，免議。

translations.literal: Luo Yangxing was denounced for greed and collusion with bandits; the accusation implicated Chongya, but the verdict found it unsubstantiated and he was exempted from prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yangxing was denounced for greed and collusion with bandits. The accusation implicated Chongya, but the case was judged unfounded and he was cleared.

sentences.zh: 給事中莊憲祖劾崇雅衰庸，崇雅疏乞罷，留之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhuang Xianzu impeached Chongya as feeble and incompetent; Chongya memorialized asking to be dismissed, but he was kept in office.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhuang Xianzu impeached Chongya as feeble and incompetent. Chongya memorialized asking to resign, but he was kept in office.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 六年，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 八年，調戶部，加少保。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and made Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and made Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 十年，引疾告歸，命仍支原俸。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he cited illness and asked to return home; he was ordered to continue receiving his original salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he cited illness and asked to retire home. He was ordered to continue receiving his original salary.

sentences.zh: 旋召還。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授國史院大學士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed Grand Academician of the National History College.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was appointed Grand Academician of the National History College.

sentences.zh: 十二年，復以老乞休，加少傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he again requested retirement on grounds of age and was made Junior Mentor and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he again asked to retire because of old age and was made Junior Mentor and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 入謝，上見其老，賜御服，諭曰：「卿今還裡，服朕賜衣，如見朕也！」

translations.literal: When he came in to give thanks, the emperor saw that he was old, granted him imperial robes, and instructed: "You now return home. Wear the robe I give you, and it will be as if you see me!"
translations.idiomatic: When he came to give thanks, the emperor saw how old he was, granted him imperial robes, and said: "You are going home now. Wear the robe I give you, and it will be as though you see me!"

sentences.zh: 臨行，復召見，賜茶，慰以溫語，命大學士車克送之。

translations.literal: As he was about to leave, the emperor summoned him again, granted him tea, comforted him with warm words, and ordered Grand Secretary Che Ke to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: As he was leaving, the emperor summoned him again, gave him tea, comforted him with kind words, and ordered Grand Secretary Che Ke to see him off.

sentences.zh: 十三年，敕存問。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year an edict was sent to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year an edict was sent to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 康熙五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 明福王時，定從賊案，崇雅與衛周祚、高爾儼皆與。

translations.literal: During the reign of the Ming Prince of Fu, in the verdict of following the rebels, Chongya, Wei Zhouzuo, and Gao Eryan were all implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming Prince of Fu, in the case finding officials guilty of following the rebels, Chongya, Wei Zhouzuo, and Gao Eryan were all implicated.

sentences.zh: 衛周祚，山西曲沃人。

translations.literal: Wei Zhouzuo was a native of Quwo in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhouzuo came from Quwo in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，官戶部郎中。

translations.literal: A jinshi of Chongzhen of Ming, he served as Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi under Chongzhen and served as a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，授吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he was appointed Director in the Ministry of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi he was appointed a director in the Ministry of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 再遷刑部侍郎，疏言：「各省逮捕土寇，坐輒數十人，請飾鞫訊得實，具獄詞解部。

translations.literal: After a second promotion he became Vice Minister of Justice and memorialized, saying: "When the provinces arrest local bandits, dozens are implicated in each case. I request that interrogation be properly conducted until the facts are established and full records be sent to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: After a further promotion he became Vice Minister of Justice and memorialized: "When provinces arrest local bandits, dozens are implicated in each case. I ask that interrogation be properly conducted until the facts are established and full records sent to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 京師多訐訟，請嚴反坐罪。

translations.literal: In the capital there are many false accusations; I request that counter-charge penalties be strictly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is rife with false accusations; I ask that counter-charge penalties be strictly enforced.

sentences.zh: 功臣犯法，請復收贖之令。」

translations.literal: When meritorious officials break the law, I request that the order allowing commutation by payment be restored."
translations.idiomatic: When meritorious officials break the law, I ask that the order allowing commutation by payment be restored."

sentences.zh: 調吏部，疏言：「六部司屬，請每歲令堂官糾舉黜陟。」

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Civil Appointments and memorialized, saying: "For the subordinate officials of the Six Ministries, I request that each year the department heads investigate them and promote or dismiss them accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Civil Appointments and memorialized: "For subordinate officials in the Six Ministries, I ask that each year the department heads investigate them and recommend promotions and dismissals.

sentences.zh: 「疆圉新闢，招民百名，即授知縣，暫委各官，即予本職，乃一時權宜計。

translations.literal: In newly opened frontier territories, recruiting one hundred settlers and immediately appointing them county magistrates, or temporarily assigning them various posts and immediately granting substantive rank, was only a temporary expedient.
translations.idiomatic: In newly opened frontier territories, recruiting one hundred settlers and immediately appointing them county magistrates, or temporarily assigning them to various posts and immediately granting substantive rank, was only a temporary expedient.

sentences.zh: 請試以文義，有不嫻者，招民改武職，暫委授佐雜。」

translations.literal: I request that they be tested in literary and administrative competence; those not proficient should, as recruited settlers, be transferred to military posts or temporarily assigned to assistant and miscellaneous ranks."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they be tested in literary and administrative competence. Those who are not proficient should, as recruited settlers, be transferred to military posts or temporarily assigned to assistant and miscellaneous ranks."

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All these proposals were sent down to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All of these proposals were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 擢尚書，歷工、吏二部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister and served in the Ministries of Works and Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to ministerial rank and served in the Ministries of Works and Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授文淵閣大學士，兼刑部尚書，改國史院。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Grand Academician of the Wenyuan Pavilion and concurrently Minister of Justice, then transferred to the National History College.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made Grand Academician of the Wenyuan Pavilion and concurrently Minister of Justice, then transferred to the National History College.

sentences.zh: 以葬兄週胤乞假還。

translations.literal: He asked leave to return home to bury his elder brother Zhou Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for leave to return home and bury his elder brother Zhou Yin.

sentences.zh: 復起授保和殿大學士，兼戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Recalled to office, he was appointed Grand Academician of the Baohe Hall and concurrently Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Grand Academician of the Baohe Hall and concurrently Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以疾乞休。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire because of illness.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年，卒，諡文清。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi he died, with the posthumous name Wenqing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year of Kangxi and was given the posthumous name Wenqing.

sentences.zh: 周祚居鄉謹厚，聖祖稱之。

translations.literal: Zhouzuo lived in his home district with careful integrity, and the Shenzu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouzuo lived in his home district with careful integrity, and the Shenzu praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 西巡，遣大臣酹其墓。

translations.literal: During the western tour, the emperor sent a high minister to pour libation at his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: During his western tour the emperor sent a high minister to pour libation at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 週胤，明崇禎七年進士，官御史。

translations.literal: Zhou Yin became a jinshi in the seventh year of Chongzhen of Ming and served as Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yin received his jinshi in the seventh year of Chongzhen under the Ming and served as a censor.

sentences.zh: 順治初，授原官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he was granted his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shunzhi reign he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 官至兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually rose to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 高爾儼，直隸靜海人。

translations.literal: Gao Eryan was a native of Jinghai in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Eryan came from Jinghai in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎十二年進士，官編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twelfth year of Chongzhen of Ming, he served as Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi in the twelfth year of Chongzhen under the Ming and served as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 順治初，授秘書院侍講學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he was appointed Lecturing Academician of the Secretariat College.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shunzhi reign he was appointed Lecturing Academician of the Secretariat College.

sentences.zh: 遷侍郎，歷禮、吏二部，擢吏部尚書，加太子太保。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister, served in the Ministries of Rites and Civil Appointments, was then promoted to Minister of Civil Appointments, and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister, served in the Ministries of Rites and Civil Appointments, rose to Minister of Civil Appointments, and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 九年，為御史吳達所論，乞罷。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was impeached by Censor Wu Da and asked to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Censor Wu Da impeached him and he asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 旋起補弘文院大學士。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was recalled and appointed Grand Academician of the Hongwen College.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and appointed Grand Academician of the Hongwen College.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒，贈少保，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died; he was granted Junior Guardian posthumously, with the posthumous name Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year and was posthumously granted Junior Guardian, with the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 張端，山東掖縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Duan was a native of Ye County in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Duan came from Ye County in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 父忻，明天啟五年進士，官至刑部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Xin became a jinshi in the fifth year of Tianqi of Ming and rose to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin received his jinshi in the fifth year of Tianqi under the Ming and rose to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 端，明崇禎十六年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: Duan became a jinshi in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen of Ming and was made a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Duan received his jinshi in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen and was made a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 李自成入京師，端從忻皆降。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng entered the capital, Duan and Xin both submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng entered the capital, both Zhang Duan and his father Xin submitted.

sentences.zh: 順治初，忻以養性薦，授天津巡撫。

translations.literal: In the early Shunzhi period, Xin was recommended by Yangxing and appointed Governor of Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shunzhi period, Xin was recommended by Luo Yangxing and appointed Governor of Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 端亦以薦授弘文院檢討。

translations.literal: Duan was also recommended and appointed Reviser of the Hongwen College.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Duan was also recommended and appointed Reviser of the Hongwen College.

sentences.zh: 三遷為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十年，授國史院大學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was appointed Grand Academician of the National History College.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed Grand Academician of the National History College.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒，贈太子太保，諡文安。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he died and was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he died and was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 忻以靜海土寇亂罷，後端卒。

translations.literal: Xin was dismissed because of bandit turmoil in Jinghai; Duan died later.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was dismissed over bandit unrest in Jinghai; Zhang Duan died later.

sentences.zh: 養性，崇禎時官錦衣衛都指揮使，頗用事。

translations.literal: Yangxing, in the Chongzhen period, served as Commander-in-Chief of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and wielded considerable power.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yangxing had served as Commander-in-Chief of the Embroidered Uniform Guard under Chongzhen and wielded considerable power.

sentences.zh: 大學士吳甡戍，周延儒死，皆有力。

translations.literal: Grand Academician Wu Shen was banished and Zhou Yanru died—both were his doing.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Academician Wu Shen was banished and Zhou Yanru died—both outcomes owed much to his influence.

sentences.zh: 來降，授總督。

translations.literal: He came to submit and was appointed Governor-General.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted to the Qing and was appointed Governor-General.

sentences.zh: 尋坐事罷，仍加太子太傅、左都督，進太子太師。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was dismissed for an offense, but was still granted Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Left Commander-in-Chief, and advanced to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dismissed for an offense but was still granted Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Left Commander-in-Chief, and advanced to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 求自效，授浙江掌印都司。

translations.literal: Seeking to prove his merit, he was appointed Seal-Holding Commander of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to prove his worth, he was appointed Seal-Holding Commander of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：世祖既親政，銳意求治，諸臣在相位，宜有閎規碩畫足以輔新運者。

translations.literal: The commentator says: After Shizu personally took power, he was keen to seek good governance; the ministers in chief office ought to have had grand designs sufficient to assist the new mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: After the Shunzhi Emperor took personal rule, he was keen to seek good governance. Ministers in chief office ought to have offered grand designs sufficient to assist the new mandate.

sentences.zh: 如蔣赫德請懲貪蠹；

translations.literal: Such as Jiang Hede's request to punish corrupt predators;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Hede asked to punish corrupt predators;

sentences.zh: 權首請田賦循萬曆舊額，並罷祖軍、民壯；

translations.literal: Quan was first to ask that land tax follow the old Wanli quota and to abolish hereditary military households and civilian braves;
translations.idiomatic: Song Quan was first to ask that land tax follow the old Wanli quota and to abolish hereditary military households and civilian braves;

sentences.zh: 永吉議清兵額、卹災傷，痛陳投旗之害；

translations.literal: Yongji proposed clearing military quotas and relieving disaster victims, and bitterly set forth the harm of enrolling under the banners;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yongji proposed clearing military quotas and relieving disaster victims, and forcefully set forth the harm of enrolling under the banners;

sentences.zh: 之俊、崇雅鄭重斷獄：可謂能舉其大矣。

translations.literal: Zhijun and Chongya were scrupulous in judging cases: they may be said to have grasped the great matters.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhijun and Dang Chongya were scrupulous in judging cases—they may be said to have grasped what mattered most.

sentences.zh: 若巴哈納以細事塞明問，以漸、宮以巍科虛特擢，及額色赫、車克輩，皆鮮所建白。

translations.literal: As for Bahana, who blocked the emperor's inquiries with petty matters; Yijian and Gong, who received empty exceptional promotion on the strength of lofty examination ranks; and Esehe, Che Ke, and their kind—all offered little by way of constructive proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Bahana blocked the emperor's inquiries with petty matters; Fu Yijian and Lü Gong received hollow exceptional promotions on the strength of top examination ranks; and Esehe, Che Ke, and their like offered little by way of constructive proposals.

sentences.zh: 要其謹身奉上，亦一代風氣所由始也。

translations.literal: Yet in essentials they were careful in person and devoted to the throne—this too was where the temper of an age began.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in essentials they were careful in conduct and devoted to the throne—and that too was where the temper of an age began.
